title: lore check's schema-drift failure does not name its own remedy at the point of failure
description:
REPORTED BY opum-marketplace 2026-09-19, from a real first-upgrade, not hypothetically. Bumping their opum-lore pin v0.7.0 -> v0.8.0 made their CI install lore 0.8.0, whose new committed-schema-drift check (LCLI-539) failed with EXIT 6 ON ALL SEVEN of their profile schemas at once -- because their committed .lore/schemas/*.json predated the check. They resolved it by running `lore schema export` and committing the result, and explicitly said it is not a bug report against lore but worth a release note or a doctor-style heads-up for other integrators.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN "ADD A RELEASE NOTE". The tool already knows the answer and does not say it where it is needed. `lore schema --help` reads, verbatim: "Export the profile's editor JSON Schemas to .lore/schemas/ (the fix for `lore check`'s schema-drift)". So the remedy is documented -- on the command you have to already know about in order to read. The 0.8.0 CHANGELOG upgrade note said only "Regenerate the schemas to clear it" and never named `lore schema export`, which is why a competent integrator had to derive it.

FIXED ALREADY, PARTIALLY: the CHANGELOG upgrade note now names the command, says to commit the regenerated files, and records opum-marketplace's measurement (7/7 schemas, exit 6, first bump past 0.8.0). That helps someone reading the changelog. It does NOT help someone reading a red CI log, which is where they actually are.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and is the part worth doing: make `lore check`'s schema-drift finding NAME ITS OWN REMEDY in the failure output -- "run `lore schema export` and commit .lore/schemas/" -- so the person who meets it never has to find a changelog, a task id, or another command's --help. Every other lore error in this codebase carries a "hint" field; this finding should too. That is the fix that removes the judgement rather than documenting it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ONE CONSUMER: this fires ONCE PER CONSUMER, on their first bump past 0.8.0, on content they did not touch, across every type simultaneously. It is maximally alarming and minimally self-explanatory at exactly the moment someone is deciding whether the upgrade is safe. opum-marketplace worked it out; they also had the advantage of a direct channel to the releasing session.

Not a regression and not a reason to hold 0.8.0 -- the check is correct and the drift it reports was real and previously unreported.
plan: 1. Name the full remedy (run `lore schema export` AND commit `.lore/schemas/`) in the missing/stale/orphaned schema-drift findings, in the sibling inline-hint idiom.
2. Pin it in test/schema-drift.test.ts (unit + runCheck integration), mutation-tested red.
3. Record it under CHANGELOG [Unreleased]; leave the spec historical quote alone (it snapshots the pre-stamp message).
4. Gates: full bun test suite, lint, typecheck, lore check. Review, record, land.
implementationNotes: Completed on branch fix/LCLI-545-schema-drift-remedy. FINDING ON THE BRIEF: "does not name its own remedy at the point of failure" is not true of the current output -- the missing/stale/orphaned messages have named `lore schema export` since LCLI-539 (commit bad5f384, landed 2026-09-18), the day BEFORE this task was filed (2026-09-19), so the genuine gap was the COMMIT step. Also "every other lore error carries a hint field" holds for thrown LoreError (src/errors.ts), NOT for check findings: a finding is {severity, rule, message} (src/core/finding.ts) and the siblings name their remedy as an INLINE suffix built from a local `hint` variable (src/core/check.ts:766/776/817). FIX: each drift finding now names the full remedy in that same inline-hint idiom -- "run `lore schema export` and commit `.lore/schemas/`", and the prune-and-commit form for an orphaned schema; unattributable still advises no command. EVIDENCE: test/schema-drift.test.ts pins the full remedy in the pure comparison AND the runCheck integration path; reverting src/core/check.ts to the pre-change wording reds all five new assertions (control 30 pass). GATES: full suite 4976 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; lint, typecheck, lore check all exit 0 (one pre-existing agent-profile capacity warning). LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: the quote at docs/specs/committed-schema-generator-stamp.md:24 -- that Summary is a snapshot of the PRE-stamp message (its "two outcomes" line predates LCLI-565 third outcome), so rewriting the quote would retro-fit a historical narrative.
finalSummary: lore check schema-drift findings (missing/stale/orphaned) now name the full remedy at the point of failure: "run `lore schema export` and commit `.lore/schemas/`" (prune-and-commit for an orphaned schema). Why: the old text named the command but not the commit, which is the step that actually clears the drift and the one opum-marketplace had to derive after their first bump failed on 7/7 schemas they had never touched. Verified by test/schema-drift.test.ts (pure + runCheck integration pins), mutation-tested red; full suite 4976 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; lint, typecheck and lore check green. Run job-133g1fq.
